posts.title: Quiet compounding
posts.excerpt: Most of the work that matters happens without applause. The trick is learning to trust the slope.
content: There's a version of progress that looks like nothing is happening. Spreadsheets barely move. Revenue ticks up by single digits. The product feels the same on the surface.
But underneath, systems are tightening. Relationships deepen. You learn which decisions repeat and which ones were noise. That slope — barely visible week to week — is where compounding lives.
I try to write when I notice one of those small shifts. Not to perform insight, but to mark the moment before it disappears into the next sprint.
